info.title: World Radio League API
info.summary: Read and write amateur radio contacts in a World Radio League logbook.
info.description:
Log contacts into World Radio League from your own software, and read them back.

## Getting a key

Sign in to World Radio League, open **Integrations → Developer API**, and choose
**Generate API key**. The key is shown once and stored hashed, so it cannot be
recovered afterwards. One key covers your whole account — it is not per logbook.

## Authenticating

Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer wrl_live_...`, or as `X-API-Key`. Both work.
If you send both they must match.

**Keep the key server-side.** These endpoints deliberately send no CORS headers, so a
browser cannot call them directly — an API key in a front-end bundle is a leaked key.

## Responses

Every response, success or failure, is `{ "data": ..., "meta": ..., "error": ... }`,
so one unwrapper handles everything. Error `code` values are stable and safe to branch
on; `message` text is not. Every response carries `X-Request-Id` — quote it in support
requests.

## Rate limits

60 writes and 120 reads per minute; 5,000 writes and 20,000 reads per day.

**Reads and writes have separate budgets.** Reading does not consume write quota, and
a write does not consume read quota. `GET`, `HEAD` and unmatched paths count as reads;
`POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` count as writes.

Every response issued after your quota was charged carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
`X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` — errors included, because a rejected
request that reached validation has already been charged. The values always describe
the budget for the kind of request you just made, so `Remaining` on a `POST` response
is your remaining writes, not your remaining reads. Track the two separately.

A `429` carries `Retry-After` in seconds, computed from whichever window actually
blocked you — honour it rather than retrying on a fixed timer.

## One contact per request

`POST /v1/contacts` takes exactly one contact. To upload many at once, send an ADIF
file with the Imports endpoints below.

## Bulk import (ADIF)

Upload a whole log as an ADIF file of up to 10 MB in three steps — start, upload, poll:

1. **Start:** `POST /v1/imports` with `{ "programId": "YourApp" }` (and optionally
   `logbookId`). The response carries `id` and `upload.url`.
2. **Upload:** `PUT` the raw `.adi` file to `upload.url`. This goes straight to file
   storage, so it needs no API key and works over a slow connection. The URL is valid for
   two hours.
3. **Poll:** `GET /v1/imports/{id}` every few seconds. Nothing else is needed: World Radio
   League notices the upload, checks it and queues it on its own.

`status` goes `awaiting_upload` → `uploaded` → `queued` → `processing` → `complete`. The
file is imported exactly as an import started in World Radio League would be —
duplicates are skipped, contacts are enriched and confirmed — usually within a few
minutes. A file that cannot be imported ends as `rejected`, with an `errorCode` saying
why. The import also appears in the operator's Activity Log, and its QSOs carry your
`programId`.

Imports run one at a time per account. The records in a file count against the account's
daily import budget (`limits.importContactsPerDay` in `GET /v1/me`), separate from the
write budget above, and an account may start `limits.importStartsPerDay` imports a day.
Your membership's own import allowance — the same as for imports in World Radio League —
applies on top: reaching it ends the import as `failed` with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.

## Enrichment

Enrichment is the process by which World Radio League derives missing information from
the data you provide. We prioritize the data you send us, but in the case that certain data such as DXCC ID is missing, we will attempt to derive it.

It happens a moment after the contact is stored, not during the request. A newly created
contact therefore comes back with `enrichment: "pending"`; re-read it a few seconds
later and `dxcc` and `distance` will be filled in.

Anything you supply yourself is never overwritten — if you already know the grid square
or the operator's name, send it and it is kept as-is.

post.description:
Logs a single QSO. The required fields are `programId`, `call`, `timestamp`, `freq`, `band` and `mode`.

`logbookId` is optional — omit it and the contact goes to your default logbook, so a new integration needs no setup call. Sending it is recommended once you know which logbook you want.

Your own callsign is worked out for you if you do not send `stationCallsign` — first
the logbook's default, then the callsign on your profile. It matters: it is what
duplicate detection and contact confirmation match on.

Sending an array is rejected. Use `POST /v1/imports` for bulk uploads.

**A QSO you have already logged is refused**, so sending the same contact twice — a
retry after a timeout, or re-syncing your log — never stores it twice. It counts as
already logged when your account holds a contact with the same `call`, the same
station callsign, the same band and a matching mode within 15 minutes of `timestamp`.
SSB, USB and LSB match each other, and a submode matches its parent mode (`FT4` matches
`MFSK`), but two different submodes do not (`FT4` and `JS8`). A contest logbook is checked
on its own; any other logbook is checked against all of yours. The answer is `409
DUPLICATE_CONTACT` with the stored contact's id in `error.existingContactId`: treat it
as logged. `POST /v1/imports` skips duplicates in a file by the same rule, except that
it compares the mode text exactly (SSB and USB do not match there).

If `band` disagrees with `freq`, the band the frequency implies is the one stored and
matched — so changing only `band` does not make it a different QSO.

get.description: Use this after creating a contact to pick up the enriched fields (`dxcc` and `distance`), which World Radio League derives from the callsign shortly after the contact is stored.

patch.description:
Only the fields you send are changed.

A contact cannot be moved to a different logbook — `logbookId` is rejected. Moving
one would change contest scoring and duplicate handling in ways that cannot be
recalculated safely. Delete it and create it in the target logbook instead.

Changing the time, either callsign, the band or the mode re-runs contact
confirmation against other operators' logs.

activities.summary: Replace your side's activities, leaving theirs untouched

422.description: Invalid value, or an attempt to move logbooks.

error.message: A contact cannot be moved between logbooks. Delete it and create it in the target logbook.

post.description:
Step 1 of 3 (start → upload → poll). Reserves an import and returns `upload.url`. `PUT` the raw ADIF file there — up to 10 MB, within two hours — then poll `GET /v1/imports/{id}`. There is no call to make after the upload: it is noticed, checked and queued for you.

The upload goes straight to file storage rather than through this API: send no API key with it, just the file as the body (`Content-Type: text/plain`). If a `PUT` fails part-way, send it again. Once the import is `queued`, further uploads to the same URL are ignored — the checked file is the one imported.

`logbookId` follows the same rules as on `POST /v1/contacts`: omit it to use your default logbook. `programId` is required and is stored on every imported QSO in place of any `PROGRAMID` in the file header.

One import runs at a time per account, including imports started in World Radio League; a second one is refused with `409`. Repeating the SAME request (same logbook and `programId`) while its reservation still waits returns that reservation again with a fresh `upload.url` and status `200` — so a lost response never locks you out.

`429` means not now, with `Retry-After`: many imports from your membership tier are already waiting (retry in about a minute), or this account has started `limits.importStartsPerDay` imports today (resets at 00:00 UTC).

200.description: The same request was already waiting for its file: that reservation, with a fresh `upload.url`. `meta.reused` is true.

201.description: Reserved. Upload the file to `upload.url`, then poll the import.

404.description: No such logbook, or it is not yours.

409.description: Another import is running, or a different import is waiting for its file, or the logbook is locked.

error.message: An ADIF import is already running for this account.

get.description:
Step 3 of 3. Poll this after uploading — every few seconds is plenty.

`status` moves `awaiting_upload` → `uploaded` (the file arrived and is being checked) → `queued` → `processing` → `complete` or `complete_with_errors`, and `counts` fill in as the file is processed. Stop polling on `complete`, `complete_with_errors`, `failed`, `rejected`, `expired` or `cancelled`.

`rejected` means the file was not imported and nothing was charged; `errorCode` says why. `expired` means no file arrived within two hours.

200.description: A page of logbooks, newest first.

patch.description: Only the fields you send are changed.

delete.description: The logbook must contain no contacts. Deleting a logbook full of contacts would cascade into a large amount of background work, so it is not offered here — delete the contacts first, or remove the logbook inside World Radio League, which handles bulk deletion in the background.

error.hint: Delete its contacts first, or remove the logbook in World Radio League.

HeaderApiKey.name: X-API-Key
HeaderApiKey.description: `X-API-Key: wrl_live_...` — equivalent to the bearer form.

Id.name: id
Id.description: Resource id. Unknown ids and ids belonging to another account both return 404.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
Pass `meta.nextCursor` from the previous response verbatim to get the next page. A null `nextCursor` means you have reached the end.

Cursors are **opaque** — do not parse, construct or modify them. They encode both the sort timestamp and a unique tiebreaker, which is what stops contacts sharing a timestamp from being skipped at a page boundary; ADIF minute-precision times make that routine. A hand-built cursor cannot express a boundary safely and is rejected with `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

data.description: The payload, or null on failure.

code.description: Stable identifier. Branch on this, not on `message`.

field.description: The field at fault, when there is one.

existingContactId.description: `DUPLICATE_CONTACT` only: the stored contact your request repeats.

nextCursor.description: Opaque. Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null means no more rows. Results are ordered by timestamp descending, tiebroken by id, so paging is stable and never skips or repeats a row.

uid.description: Your World Radio League user id.

email.description: Your login email. Null only if your profile could not be read.

publicEmail.description: The email you chose to show on your public WRL profile. Null when unset, in which case your profile shows your login email.

defaultLogbook.description: Where a contact goes when you omit `logbookId`. Check this once at setup: a null `logbookId` means such a request will be refused with `LOGBOOK_REQUIRED`, and you can tell the operator what to fix before they try to log a QSO.

logbookId.description: Null when no destination can be resolved.

resolution.description: `configured` — explicitly chosen. `sole` — the only usable logbook. `ambiguous` — several exist and none is chosen, so send `logbookId`. `none` — no unlocked logbook exists; create one first.

maxContactsPerRequest.description: Contacts accepted per POST. Currently always 1.

importContactsPerDay.description: ADIF records this ACCOUNT may import per UTC day through `POST /v1/imports`, across all its keys. 0 means bulk import is not available. Your membership's own import allowance, the same as for imports in World Radio League, still applies on top.

importStartsPerDay.description: Imports this account may start per UTC day, counting ones whose file is later rejected.

quota.description: Read budget only. GET /v1/me is itself a read, so it reports the counters it just charged; your write budget is separate and unaffected by calling this endpoint. Read the write figures from the X-RateLimit-* headers on your next write.

defaultCallSign.description: Used as `myCallsign` when a contact does not supply one.

QsoTimestamp.description:
When the contact happened, in UTC. An ISO-8601 string without a timezone is treated as UTC — amateur radio logs UTC by convention, so a local time would be silently wrong.

ADIF splits this across `QSO_DATE` and `TIME_ON` and has no combined field; one instant is friendlier for a JSON API, so `timestamp` is the one place this API deliberately leaves the ADIF vocabulary. The ADIF pair is accepted too, under ADIF's own names, for callers translating straight from an ADIF record.

timeOn.description: ADIF TIME_ON — HHMM or HHMMSS. HHMM is padded to :00 seconds.

type.description: Activity programme code — POTA, SOTA, IOTA, WWFF. Optional when the reference exists under only one programme.

ref.description: The location's reference, as the programme publishes it. Case is normalised.

isPrimary.description: At most one per side. Defaults to the first entry in the list.

name.description: The location's name in World Radio League.

ContactCreate.description: Unknown fields are rejected rather than ignored, so a misspelled name never silently loses data.

programId.description: **Required.** The logger, converter or utility posting this contact — the equivalent of ADIF `PROGRAMID`. Send a short program name; it is recorded against the contact so the operator can see which application logged a QSO, and is not returned in responses.

logbookId.description:
Optional but recommended. Must be one of your own logbooks.

Omit it (or send null) and the contact goes to your default logbook: the one chosen under Integrations → Developer API, or your only logbook if you have just one. If you have several and have chosen none, the request is refused with `LOGBOOK_REQUIRED` rather than guessed at — a contact cannot be moved between logbooks afterwards, so a wrong guess would be permanent.

`meta.logbookResolution` on the response reports which rule applied, and `GET /v1/me` reports your default before you write anything.

call.description: The station you worked. Case is normalised. Portable and reciprocal forms are accepted: W1AW, W1AW/4, DL/W1AW, VP2E/W1AW/QRP.

band.description: Band as "20m", "20", 20 or "70cm". Must be a band World Radio League recognises (2200m down to 23cm); an unrecognised or malformed value is rejected. If it disagrees with the frequency, the frequency wins and a warning is returned in `meta.warnings`.

mode.description: Mode or submode of the contact. World Radio League stores a single mode field, so send the submode when you want to be specific. For JS8 contacts it is preferred to send "JS8" — World Radio League understands that as ADIF MODE = MFSK, SUBMODE = JS8.

stationCallsign.description: Station callsign. Defaults to the account callsign if not specified: the logbook's default callsign is used first, then the callsign on your profile.

myGridsquare.description: Your own Maidenhead locator: 2, 4, 6 or 8 characters (e.g. "FN31", "FN31pr").

gridsquare.description: Maidenhead locator of the contacted station: 2, 4, 6 or 8 characters (e.g. "FN31", "FN31pr").

state.description: State/province of the contacted station. An abbreviation is preferred where possible ("TX" rather than "Texas").

operator.description: Callsign of the operator who is operating the station. Defaults to the account callsign if not specified.

myActivities.description:
Activity locations you were operating FROM — the activator's side. A park, summit, island or reserve already known to World Radio League, identified by its reference (e.g. "US-0662"). Up to 7 per contact.

`type` may be omitted when the reference exists under only one programme; where it does not (the same reference can exist as both POTA and WWFF) the request is refused with `AMBIGUOUS_ACTIVITY_REFERENCE` rather than guessed at. An IOTA reference covers a group of islands and is accepted as the group; the `name` returned is one island of it. A reference World Radio League does not know is refused with `UNKNOWN_ACTIVITY_REFERENCE` — nothing is stored, so the contact is not created with the activity silently missing.

`isPrimary` marks the location a map pin and the activity breakdowns use. At most one per side; if you flag none, the first entry in the list is used.

theirActivities.description:
Activity locations the station you worked was operating from — the hunter's view of the same thing. Up to 7 per contact.

`type` may be omitted when the reference exists under only one programme; where it does not (the same reference can exist as both POTA and WWFF) the request is refused with `AMBIGUOUS_ACTIVITY_REFERENCE` rather than guessed at. An IOTA reference covers a group of islands and is accepted as the group; the `name` returned is one island of it. A reference World Radio League does not know is refused with `UNKNOWN_ACTIVITY_REFERENCE` — nothing is stored, so the contact is not created with the activity silently missing.

`isPrimary` marks the location a map pin and the activity breakdowns use. At most one per side; if you flag none, the first entry in the list is used.

ContactUpdate.description: `logbookId` is not accepted — a contact cannot change logbook.

band.description: Must be a recognised band. Sent alone (no `freq`), it is validated directly, since there is no frequency to reconcile it against.

mode.description: Mode or submode of the contact. World Radio League stores a single mode field, so send the submode when you want to be specific. For JS8 contacts it is preferred to send "JS8" — World Radio League understands that as ADIF MODE = MFSK, SUBMODE = JS8.

gridsquare.description: Maidenhead locator of the contacted station: 2, 4, 6 or 8 characters (e.g. "FN31", "FN31pr").

state.description: State/province of the contacted station. An abbreviation is preferred where possible ("TX" rather than "Texas").

operator.description: Callsign of the operator who is operating the station. Defaults to the account callsign if not specified.

`type` may be omitted when the reference exists under only one programme; where it does not (the same reference can exist as both POTA and WWFF) the request is refused with `AMBIGUOUS_ACTIVITY_REFERENCE` rather than guessed at. `isPrimary` marks the location a map pin and the activity breakdowns use. At most one per side; if you flag none, the first entry in the list is used.

**A PATCH replaces this side in full.** Send the complete list you want to end up with. Omit the field to leave the side untouched, or send `[]` to clear it. The other side is never affected.

An IOTA reference covers a group of islands and is accepted as the group; the `name` returned is one island of it. A reference World Radio League does not know is refused with `UNKNOWN_ACTIVITY_REFERENCE` — nothing is stored, so the contact is not created with the activity silently missing.

Contact.description:
Fields marked *enriched* are derived by World Radio League from the data you provided (see Enrichment in the overview) shortly after the contact is created. Anything you supplied yourself is never overwritten.

`programId` is not listed here: it is required on create and is recorded against the contact, but it is never returned. See `ContactCreate`.

mode.description: Mode or submode of the contact. World Radio League stores a single mode field, so send the submode when you want to be specific. For JS8 contacts it is preferred to send "JS8" — World Radio League understands that as ADIF MODE = MFSK, SUBMODE = JS8.

operator.description: Callsign of the operator who is operating the station.

gridsquare.description: Maidenhead locator of the contacted station: 2, 4, 6 or 8 characters (e.g. "FN31", "FN31pr").

state.description: State/province of the contacted station. An abbreviation is preferred where possible ("TX" rather than "Texas").

dxcc.description: *enriched* — ADIF DXCC entity code. Country, continent and flag are all derivable from this and are deliberately not duplicated here.

myGridsquare.description: Your own Maidenhead locator: 2, 4, 6 or 8 characters (e.g. "FN31", "FN31pr").

isDuplicate.description: Set by World Radio League when it matches another contact in your log.

myActivities.description: Activity locations you were operating FROM — the activator's side. A park, summit, island or reserve already known to World Radio League, identified by its reference (e.g. "US-0662"). Up to 7 per contact. Always present; empty when there are none. Ordered primary first.

theirActivities.description: Activity locations the station you worked was operating from — the hunter's view of the same thing. Up to 7 per contact. Always present; empty when there are none. Ordered primary first.

enrichment.description: Always `pending` on create: `dxcc` and `distance` are derived from the callsign within a few seconds of the contact being stored. Re-read the contact to see them.

programId.description: The software sending the file, e.g. "Ham2k". Stored on every imported QSO in place of the file's own PROGRAMID, so the operator's log shows where they came from.

logbookId.description: Destination logbook. Omit to use your default logbook.

status.description: `awaiting_upload` until the file arrives (`expired` if two hours pass first), `uploaded` while it is checked, then `queued`, `processing`, and one of `complete`, `complete_with_errors`, `failed` or `cancelled`. `rejected` means the file was refused before import — see `errorCode`.

logbookId.description: Null once the logbook has been deleted.

recordCount.description: Records counted in the file at completion — what was charged.

progress.description: Percent processed, 0–100, once the import has started.

counts.description: Filled in as the file is processed; null until then.

duplicates.description: Already in the account, so skipped.

errorCode.description:
Why the import did not go through, when it did not.

With `status: rejected` (nothing imported, nothing charged): `FILE_TOO_LARGE` — over 10 MB; `NO_RECORDS` — no record ending in `<eor>`; `EXCEEDS_DAILY_LIMIT` — more records than your whole daily import budget, so split the file; `IMPORT_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` — the account's import budget for today is used up, start again after 00:00 UTC; `KEY_REVOKED` — the API key was revoked; `LOGBOOK_DELETED` — the logbook was deleted before the file was imported; `INTERNAL` — the file could not be read after several tries.

With `status: failed`: `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — the account's membership import allowance was reached during the import.

expiresAt.description: When the upload window closes, while the import is awaiting its file.

url.description: PUT the raw ADIF file here — no API key, `Content-Type: text/plain`.

Unauthorized.description: The key is missing, malformed, unknown, or revoked. `KEY_REVOKED` means generate a new one.

error.message: The API key is not valid.
error.hint: Check for truncation or extra whitespace when copying the key.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but not permitted: the account's tier is not allowed to use the API, a missing scope, or a source address the key is not allowed to be used from.

error.message: This account's tier is not permitted to use the API.
error.hint: The key stays valid — if your tier changes, access is restored automatically.

NotFound.description: No such resource. Returned identically whether the id does not exist or belongs to another account.

error.message: Expected an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (e.g. "2026-07-30T14:35:00Z") or ADIF form.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Honour `Retry-After` — it is computed from the window that actually blocked you, so a daily exhaustion does not tell you to retry in seconds.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Per-minute ceiling for this request's kind — the write limit on a write, the read limit on a read.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Remaining units in that same budget. Reads and writes are counted separately.

InternalError.description: Something went wrong on our side. Quote `requestId` when reporting it.
